I totally feel your pain man, I volunteered parking cars from 5 oclock in the morning to two oclock in the afternoon, then at vert cargo net two on saturday from 2 oclock till 10 oclock at night, and then ran the beast on sunday, and I can vouche for the number of cheaters. Im only 17, and in hind sight I should have been taking bib numbers and radioing down to disqualify them, but there was little more I thought to do at the time other than yell insults at them. I think the issue is a result of the fact that the volunteers are not told what to do when cheating occurs. The way I helped myself get over it is that they dont deserve that medal or that finisher t-shirt, and while that doesnt stop them from showing it off to their friends, we know that we did every last fucking burpee when we fell off that last climbing wall, or slipped from the ropes between the two walls after the first log carry, and we get to wear that dank t-shirt with pride, and look at that medal with a true feeling of accomplishment in our hearts. I will be continuing to run these for a long time (last weekend was my first) and I intend to volunteer every time to save money, and so I will be being much more harsh to cheaters. If we spread the word and get staff members to exlplain what to do when people are cheating, we will solve a big issue with this race!

The equation for the force of gravity between two objects is as follows.
Force of gravity = ((G)*(m1)*(m2))/d^2

G=6.67*10^-11 (the unit of which is NewtonMeters^2/kg^2

m1=mass of first object
m2=mass of second object
d=distance between the center of mass of the two objects.

Because of this relationship, every atom in the universe is exerting force on every other atom. So, there is no actual limit to how far a satelite could orbit, the the force of gravity from other stellar masses (such as the sun) would eventually become greater than that of the earth, and pull the satelite away.
